accepted_taxonomy.source: Kew Plants of the World Online

project_inclusion.learning_reason: One of the most important Central Texas prairie grasses and a high-value comparison against invasive King Ranch bluestem and native silver bluestem.

target_zone_range.evidence_note: Kew accepts the species as native to Texas. Hagenbuch & Lemke examined Texas Hill Country herbarium specimens from six unambiguous project target-zone counties, including Hays.

look_here_first: When it is flowering, look at the branching pattern before staring at individual spikelets: little bluestem makes numerous lateral branches, and each branch terminates in a single spikelet-bearing raceme. Then check the laterally compressed, keeled sheath.
project_tracker_diagnostic: Dense perennial bunchgrass with compressed/keeled sheaths; flowering culms have many lateral branches that each terminate in a single raceme. Nodes are usually glabrous, unlike hairy-node/papilla-hair characters of KR bluestem.

morphology_keys.habit: Cespitose, well-defined bunches; rhizomes absent or short; culms commonly 50–200 cm in Hill Country material.
morphology_keys.sheaths: Laterally compressed and keeled; surface varies from glabrous to hairy.
morphology_keys.ligule: Membranous, about 1–3 mm, obtuse with an erose/dentate-looking margin.
morphology_keys.leaf_blades: Linear, usually 1.5–4(–6) mm wide; margins scabrous; blades often fold.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Numerous lateral branches; each branch terminates in a solitary raceme of paired spikelets. Mature seed heads become silvery/fluffy from hairs and awns.
morphology_keys.seasonal_color: Basal shoots often bluish/glaucous with red streaking; mature plants commonly become reddish/coppery in late summer and fall.
best_field_traits: single raceme at the end of each of many lateral branches

lookalikes.separator: KR bluestem has terminal clusters of multiple racemes rather than little bluestem's single raceme at the end of each of many lateral branches. KR also commonly shows papilla-based hairs just above the collar and short hairs around the nodes.

Silver bluestem forms a compact terminal cluster/panicle of many conspicuously silky racemes; little bluestem spreads solitary racemes along numerous lateral branches. Vegetatively, little bluestem has distinctly compressed/keeled sheaths.

diagnostic_image_roles: mature raceme and fluffy seed detail

photo_strategy.selection_logic: Teach the single-raceme-on-lateral-branch architecture first, then the compressed sheath and late-season habit.

ecology.habitat: Prairies, grasslands, open woodlands, slopes, old fields, and woodland edges; common in Central Texas prairie remnants.
ecology.season: Warm-season; flowering and conspicuous seed heads mainly late summer through fall.
